top_choice_rationale: Nitrogenase with Rees, Seefeldt and Dean is the most mature and separable achievement on the slate: the MoFe protein and FeMo-cofactor structures, the carbide and ligand-bound states have been reproduced by independent groups over about three decades, and Seefeldt's kinetics defined the ATP-coupled electron-transfer cycle while Dean's genetics made the protein and cofactor biosynthesis tractable. The citation must stop at structure, cofactor chemistry and the electron-transfer cycle, since the N2 reduction mechanism is unresolved. The Einsle variant (P005) is nearly as defensible and ranks second; PROTACs (P002) follow as a real design principle with no approved drug and an unresolved glue lineage.
recusal_note: No connection to any B009 candidate, but I work on proton transfer in cytochrome c oxidase, so my interest in biological energy conversion may shade my judgement; Xiaodong Zou is a Stockholm University colleague, which is not a tie to any candidate.
